title: 2019 HMMT November Team Problem 1
statement: Each person in Cambridge drinks a (possibly different) 12 ounce mixture of water and apple juice, where each drink has a positive amount of both liquids. Marc McGovern, the mayor of Cambridge, drinks \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the total amount of water drunk and \(\frac{1}{8}\) of the total amount of apple juice drunk. How many people are in Cambridge?

solutions.text:
Answer: 7
The total amount of liquid drunk must be more than 6 times of the amount that Marc drinks but less than 8 times of the amount that Marc drinks. Therefore, the number of people in Cambridge is more than 6 but less than 8 , so it must be 7 .
